prev_main.title: Read What Light There Is (The Cartographer and the Fog)
prev_main.source_path: ~/Documents/SunoArchive/wav/2026-11/3cacf987 Read What Light There Is (The Cartographer and the Fog).wav
first_lines: Once there was a cartographer who lived her quiet days in a country swathed from edge to edge in fog’s unlifting haze. The fog was not a flaw in it — no error and no slog; it was the country’s nature, just its own peculiar shlog.

So the people, moving through it, kept to those they held most near, and trusted by the closeness of a face they saw was clear. Their faith was bound to proximity, to kin within their reach — but the rulers lived far off in white, past sight or call of each.
